newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian justice minister could be PM, Dehaene says.
newsitem.headline: Belgian justice minister could be PM, Dehaene says.

text.p: Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene on Tuesday singled out Justice Minister Stefaan De Clerck as a potential successor.
"There are more (politicians) who are eligible for it but De Clerck is certainly one of them," Dehaene told Belgium's Humo magazine when asked whether De Clerck would be his successor.

Asked who deserved the title of minister of the year, Dehaene said De Clerck, a fellow member of his Christian Democrat CVP party had proved he was "carved from the right wood" to tackle difficult problems like justice.
"He does that perfectly and he therefore gets my full support," Dehaene said.
According to a recent biography, Dehaene has told close friends he does not want to stand for a third term in office after the country's next elections in 1999.
De Clerck has won plaudits for his efforts to restore public confidence in the law after a child sex and murder scandal erupted last August.
He has promised better communication between the judiciary and the public and extra spending on its infrastructure.
Police have so far found the bodies of four girls in connection with the case, and are searching for seven more children. Two other girls rescued alive from a hidden cell had been sexually abused.
